editorial.headline: Forest-Area Use Services Without Changing the Forest’s Function
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers forestry services for using forest areas while keeping the area’s function and designation intact, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali PMA block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity is best understood as a forestry service category, not as a licence to redefine the land it touches. The scope is precise: it covers services in the field of using forest areas without changing the function and designation of those forest areas. In plain English, the registered business is framed around the service of enabling or managing forest-area use while the underlying forest status remains what it is. The important editorial point is the restraint built into the wording. The activity is about use within a forest-area framework, not conversion, replacement, or a new land purpose.

For founders, that distinction matters because the registered activity should match the real operating model. A company using this classification is not simply saying that it works near forests, or that forestry is part of its brand language. It is placing itself in a service role connected to the use of forest areas, with the function and designation of those areas left unchanged. The slim record opens this activity across the full scale spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not reserved in the record for only one size of operator. It can sit with a small services business or with a larger company structure, provided the business description remains inside the stated scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put plainly, the national record does not cap foreign ownership below full foreign control for this activity. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That does not create a broader operational promise beyond the record, but it does give the investor-facing reading: as a national KBLI position, this activity is open to a foreign-owned company up to the stated ceiling.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it should not be made more dramatic than the data allows. Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, but this record is not marked as blocked for Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason says the activity is PMA TERBUKA 100% with risk Menengah-Tinggi. The honest conclusion is therefore direct: a foreign-owned company can read this activity as nationally open, and the slim record does not show a Bali PMA registration block for it. The national opening and the Bali reading point in the same practical direction, so the right caution is not a hidden prohibition; it is simply disciplined classification.
